reviews.strongest_objection: Calling the runtime local can hide remote providers and execution environments.
reviews.source_limitations: Core/session inspection establishes ownership, not a single deployment topology.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: External model, MCP, connector, and remote-exec boundaries exist.
reviews.rationale: Retained wording says stateful runtime and allows delegated capabilities.

reviews.strongest_objection: Surfaces contain logic beyond thin presentation adapters.
reviews.source_limitations: Crate ownership and app-server paths do not enumerate every surface feature.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: App-server owns subscriptions, handshake, config, and compatibility behavior.
reviews.rationale: Wording now says shared core plus surface-specific transport/presentation, not identical thin clients.

reviews.strongest_objection: Context inputs and ordering change across providers, modes, and tasks.
reviews.source_limitations: Only representative turn/context paths were inspected.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: Specialized tasks add or omit fragments.
reviews.rationale: The projection claim is architectural and does not freeze an exact prompt layout.

reviews.strongest_objection: Not every user turn invokes tools or repeats sampling.
reviews.source_limitations: The main turn loop does not represent every standalone task.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: Direct completion, failure, and cancellation terminate early.
reviews.rationale: Retained wording uses may and explicitly includes other terminal paths.

reviews.strongest_objection: Some transports introduce other IDs that could be confused with model call IDs.
reviews.source_limitations: Router tests cover selected response item variants.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: No inspected generic function/custom-tool output path intentionally changes call_id.
reviews.rationale: Claim is scoped to the model function/custom-tool correlation field.

reviews.strongest_objection: Users may assume every registered hidden tool is callable by the model.
reviews.source_limitations: Source shows separate sets but not actual provider behavior for hallucinated hidden calls.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: Normal tool calling is driven by advertised schemas.
reviews.rationale: Wording distinguishes handler registration from advertisement without claiming hidden calls normally occur.

reviews.strongest_objection: An exposure check could exist upstream or in a handler not visible in the generic registry function.
reviews.source_limitations: This is a bounded negative search at one commit.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: Provider schema selection is an upstream practical restriction.
reviews.rationale: The page states only that the generic registry is not the enforcement point and names what stronger proof would require.

reviews.strongest_objection: The real policy includes reasons and amendments, not a three-state toy enum.
reviews.source_limitations: Focused on execution approval decisions.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: Additional policy metadata exists.
reviews.rationale: The guide calls the three labels a simplification and acknowledges richer details.

reviews.strongest_objection: Approval and sandboxing can be entangled in fallback/retry behavior.
reviews.source_limitations: OS-specific enforcement was not exhaustively executed in this pass.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: Distinct approval wait and sandbox construction paths remain observable.
reviews.rationale: Separate questions and enforcement points are directly supported for local command/patch paths.

reviews.strongest_objection: Remote environments can have their own sandbox, making 'not sandboxed' misleading.
reviews.source_limitations: External service implementations are outside this repository audit.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: Some remote tool hosts may enforce stronger restrictions than local Codex.
reviews.rationale: Wording says they do not automatically inherit the local sandbox and require controls at their own boundary.

reviews.strongest_objection: Pairing logic is not a uniqueness proof.
reviews.source_limitations: No global duplicate-output invariant or exhaustive transition proof was found.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: Normalization explicitly fixes absence/orphans but does not establish ∃! in every reachable state.
reviews.rationale: The exactly-one formula was stronger than the inspected implementation evidence.

reviews.strongest_objection: Raw rollout records can still contain interrupted or malformed shapes.
reviews.source_limitations: Tests cover selected normalization cases.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: The normalizer is applied when building usable model history, not retroactively to every stored byte.
reviews.rationale: Claim is now scoped to normalized model history.

reviews.strongest_objection: Cooperative cancellation does not guarantee an active process stops promptly.
reviews.source_limitations: Handler termination behavior varies.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: Cleanup and delayed termination paths exist.
reviews.rationale: Retained text describes signaling and cleanup, not instantaneous kill guarantees.

reviews.strongest_objection: Append-only implies immutable history and no repair.
reviews.source_limitations: Storage behavior may vary for future backends.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: Recorder repairs tails, updates metadata, and materializes compaction state.
reviews.rationale: All guide uses now say append-oriented and name the mutations.

reviews.strongest_objection: A loaded session may reuse cached state, and ephemeral threads may lack disk history.
reviews.source_limitations: The exact store chosen depends on configuration.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: Resume code nevertheless reconstructs a fresh live engine from available records rather than reviving task objects.
reviews.rationale: Wording allows storage variation and focuses on process/live-object identity.

reviews.strongest_objection: One-to-one persistence of all events/effects is not implemented or demonstrated.
reviews.source_limitations: No exhaustive external-effect trace was run.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: Live deltas and externally committed service actions can differ from rollout items.
reviews.rationale: Guide now says selected items according to persistence policy and separates events from records.

reviews.strongest_objection: Review, compact, and parallel tool tasks make 'one task' too absolute.
reviews.source_limitations: Task taxonomy is evolving.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: Specialized task kinds and controlled within-turn concurrency exist.
reviews.rationale: Claim is explicitly limited to the ordinary user-turn model-loop owner.

reviews.strongest_objection: An oversized prompt can still fail; boundedness is not a theorem.
reviews.source_limitations: No exhaustive proof over all providers and inputs was found.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: Compaction/truncation failure and provider-limit errors are possible.
reviews.rationale: Formula now conditions size on admission and treats failure as an allowed outcome.

reviews.strongest_objection: Events and durable items overlap enough that readers may see the distinction as artificial.
reviews.source_limitations: Not every event/item mapping was enumerated.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: Separate subscriber emission and rollout recording paths have distinct lifetimes.
reviews.rationale: The distinction is about representation/lifecycle, not denying overlap.

reviews.strongest_objection: App-server contains substantial orchestration and could be described as more than an adapter.
reviews.source_limitations: Only architectural processors were sampled.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: It owns connection, subscription, compatibility, and config workflows.
reviews.rationale: Retained wording names those concerns while locating the shared model/tool loop in core.

reviews.strongest_objection: Different transports or in-process use might bypass the wire handshake.
reviews.source_limitations: Connection tests cover supported paths, not arbitrary direct internal calls.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: Message processor enforces per-connection initialization state across transport adapters.
reviews.rationale: Claim is scoped to app-server protocol connections.

reviews.strongest_objection: Bounded queues do not imply globally bounded memory or deterministic overload timing.
reviews.source_limitations: Capacities and all auxiliary buffers were not measured.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: Other allocations exist outside the named queues.
reviews.rationale: Claim states bounded internal queues and overload behavior only.

reviews.strongest_objection: The API includes many account, config, process, plugin, and experimental methods beyond thread/turn/item.
reviews.source_limitations: The ledger audits architectural lifecycle, not the entire field catalog.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: Additional method families are extensive.
reviews.rationale: Thread/turn/item is correctly presented as the lifecycle spine, not the total API.

reviews.strongest_objection: Some approvals may be core events rather than server requests, or use tool-specific forms.
reviews.source_limitations: Not every approval variant was enumerated.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: Multiple approval methods exist.
reviews.rationale: The general bidirectional correlated-request contract is directly present.

reviews.strongest_objection: Experimental labeling is method-specific; some v2 APIs are supported.
reviews.source_limitations: Status can change after the pinned commit.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: Stable/nonexperimental methods coexist in the same document.
reviews.rationale: Wording requires per-method checking and limits instability to designated experimental APIs.

reviews.strongest_objection: Generated schemas may lag code or omit semantic constraints.
reviews.source_limitations: No schema regeneration diff was run in this pass.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: Processors/tests define runtime semantics beyond types.
reviews.rationale: Retained text assigns shapes to types/schemas and behavior to processors/tests.

reviews.strongest_objection: A working experimental websocket implementation could make 'unsupported' sound nonfunctional.
reviews.source_limitations: Support status is documentary, not a reliability benchmark.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: Websocket tests exist.
reviews.rationale: Wording carefully distinguishes existence from production support.

reviews.strongest_objection: Without Codex sandbox could be mistaken for unconstrained root execution.
reviews.source_limitations: Host account/OS controls were not modeled.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: Normal host permissions still apply.
reviews.rationale: Final wording says bypasses Codex sandbox and names the host-process boundary, not absence of all controls.

reviews.strongest_objection: Parts of protocol_v1.md have been updated and still match code.
reviews.source_limitations: Staleness is section-specific.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: The document includes current compatibility notes and newer item fields.
reviews.rationale: It remains useful but is not treated as the sole current authority.

reviews.strongest_objection: SQ/EQ may sound like a required concrete transport.
reviews.source_limitations: Historical document predates modern app-server framing.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: App-server uses JSON-RPC transport and connection processors.
reviews.rationale: Wording calls SQ/EQ a conceptual model for submission/event direction.

reviews.strongest_objection: A prose compatibility note may drift from serializer code.
reviews.source_limitations: Exact serializer tests were not separately executed.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: No contrary type representation was found in the pinned protocol definitions.
reviews.rationale: Supported at the pinned commit, with scope limited to v1 tags.

reviews.strongest_objection: Experimental could be misread as referring to all MCP usage in Codex.
reviews.source_limitations: The target document covers Codex-as-MCP-server control surface.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: Codex also consumes external MCP servers through other paths.
reviews.rationale: Final wording explicitly says Codex MCP control interface.

reviews.strongest_objection: The documentation list may outpace actual server wiring.
reviews.source_limitations: Not every method was invoked during this pass.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: The document itself subordinates authority to protocol types and server wiring.
reviews.rationale: Claim is pinned, experimental, and says maps rather than promising permanent completeness.

reviews.strongest_objection: A shared policy type might lead readers to assume uniform enforcement.
reviews.source_limitations: No cross-platform integration suite was run here.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: README documents platform-specific fallbacks, helper requirements, and representability limits.
reviews.rationale: The retained claim emphasizes nonuniform backend behavior.

reviews.strongest_objection: Some Windows policies are translated to legacy forms rather than rejected.
reviews.source_limitations: Complex path-overlap cases were not independently executed.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: README explicitly permits lossless round trips and rejects specified lossy cases.
reviews.rationale: Final wording distinguishes enforceable/lossless cases from fail-closed cases.

reviews.strongest_objection: Mathematical notation may imply proof to an unfamiliar reader.
reviews.source_limitations: No formal methods tool output exists to cite.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: The page previously called properties invariants without always separating observed from normative.
reviews.rationale: Opening and safety sections now explicitly label status and scope.

reviews.strongest_objection: The page uses informal temporal shorthand and implementation-defined functions, not only textbook notation.
reviews.source_limitations: Background links teach foundations, not this custom model.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: Eventually is not defined as a formal temporal operator here.
reviews.rationale: Final wording calls it engineering shorthand and the page defines every custom symbol locally.

reviews.strongest_objection: Responsiveness alone is insufficient without fairness and termination assumptions.
reviews.source_limitations: No temporal model or scheduler proof was constructed.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: Tools can hang, cleanup can delay, and retries/transports can fail.
reviews.rationale: The property remains pedagogically useful only as a desired conditional design hypothesis.

reviews.strongest_objection: A model could request an unrelated effect while one approval is pending, so a global execution pause is too broad.
reviews.source_limitations: Concurrency across independent calls was not exhaustively modeled.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: The approval waiter directly blocks the governed invocation, not necessarily all unrelated work.
reviews.rationale: Final claim is scoped to that governed local side effect.

reviews.strongest_objection: The repository demonstrably has heterogeneous and exceptional execution boundaries.
reviews.source_limitations: Not every extension/connector was traced.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: Remote MCP boundaries and unsandboxed experimental process/spawn contradict a universal current-state invariant.
reviews.rationale: Converted from repository theorem to explicit design requirement per tool family.

reviews.strongest_objection: Recorded history may be redacted, compacted, repaired, or incomplete as an audit.
reviews.source_limitations: Retention policies were not exhaustively traced.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: Rollout is reconstruction-oriented, not formally a compliance ledger.
reviews.rationale: Recommendation now separates reconstruction/audit policy from model projection and avoids claiming completeness.

reviews.strongest_objection: One aggregate review could conceal an incorrect label in a diagram.
reviews.source_limitations: Diagrams are abstractions and were not generated from code.
reviews.conflicting_evidence: Original labels overstated full persistence, append-only storage, and unconditional boundedness.
reviews.rationale: Those labels were corrected; the audit index documents the diagrams' deliberate omissions and the ledger separately reviews their underlying contracts.
